name: The Mighty Boosh
s: Come with us now on a journey through time and space... to the world of The Mighty Boosh … an off-the-wall adventure based on the Perrier Award-winning comedy show. The Mighty Boosh follows two zoo keepers, Howard Moon and Vince Noir, who work at "The Zoo-niverse", a dilapidated but magical zoo. paragraphs.text: The Mighty Boosh is a British surreal comedy television series written by Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding, originally broadcast on BBC Three from 2004 to 2007. Three series totalling twenty episodes were made. Set in a surreal universe, the series follows the adventures of Howard Moon (Barratt) and Vince Noir (Fielding), two eccentric and failing musicians. The pair are joined by a supporting cast of characters—shaman Naboo the Enigma (Michael Fielding), zookeeper Bob Fossil (Rich Fulcher) and Bollo the Gorilla (Dave Brown), who comprised The Mighty Boosh as a comedy group. They navigate the bizarre situations around them with elaborate musical numbers in different genres and an array of …

While beginning as a niche stage and radio act, The Mighty Boosh rapidly gained a cult following, and eventually won the Shockwaves NME Award for Best TV Show in both 2007 and 2009. Its surreal innovation earned it the 31st spot on Rotten Tomatoes' list of the 200 Best Comedy Series of All Time. In 2019, the show was ranked 98th on The Guardians list of the 100 best TV shows of the 21st century. It has been noted for its impact on mid-2000s popular culture and alternative humour.

Upon its television debut in 2004, The Mighty Boosh was identified by critics as a "comedy revolution," distinguished by its rejection of the prevailing realist sitcom trend—archetyped by The Office—in favour of "neon-soaked surrealism" and a "lo-fi, DIY aesthetic". Reviewers praised the show's "unmatched combination of imagination," noting that while the surrealism was its calling card, the series was grounded by the "warm" and "odd-couple" chemistry between Howard Moon and Vince Noir. The series led to the emergence of cult following often termed "Booshmania," particularly among the youth and "nu-rave" subcultures of the mid-2000s, although the BBC cut the budget for the third series, …

The show is regarded as a landmark in British television comedy, frequently cited as a "comedy revolution" that defined the "NME generation". However, Emma Garland of Vice described the show as moving from "supremely cool to supremely uncool" within the space of five years, as the specific cultural moment it satirised and celebrated evolved. Despite this, it has maintained a strong critical rating over time, holding an 8.4/10 on IMDb and a 100% Tomatometer score on Rotten Tomatoes.

In recent years, the show has faced scrutiny regarding its use of blackface; in 2020, Netflix removed the series from its platform over a character called "The Spirit of Jazz" in an episode titled Electro. Comedian Jack Carroll criticised the removal as "an arbitrary gesture that means [Netflix] doesn’t have to put any real work into combatting actual instances of racial discrimination." The series was kept on BBC iPlayer but a content warning was added before each episode.
